Title printed above plot: 'Utilization of ITN among pregnant women in East Africa'. X-axis label: 'Proportion by Country'. Columns printed: Study | [forest area] | ES (95% CI). Classified forest_generic: only the effect size and its CI are printed - no per-arm event/N columns, no denominators, no weight column. This is a single-arm PROPORTION meta-analysis, not a between-arm contrast, so no 2x2 exists to recover; effect_measure is 'other' because the header prints only 'ES (95% CI)' and the axis says 'Proportion'. RESOLUTION CAVEAT - this is the dominant limitation of this reading: the figure is rendered at low resolution and the row text is very small (roughly half the height of Fig3's text for the same content). The digits are readable but not crisply so, therefore nearly every study/subtotal row is marked confidence 'medium' rather than 'high', and label/year/effect/ci fields carry 'medium' field_confidence. This is deliberate: the values were read from these pixels only. I did NOT copy values across from Fig3 of the same paper to raise confidence, and I did not reconcile this figure against that one. ONE FIELD ABSTAINED: 'Kumsa Negasa et.al  (2024)' - the lower CI bound is PRINTED but I cannot resolve whether the second digit is 0 or 1 (i.e. 0.50 vs 0.51), so ci_low = 'abstain' with field_confidence 'abstain'; its point estimate 0.56 and upper bound 0.61 are legible at medium confidence. Structure: 8 country subgroups printed as bare header rows with no accompanying statistics - Ethiopia (13 studies), Kenya (5), Rwanda (4), South_Sudan (1), Sudan (1), Tanzania (4), Uganda (5), Zambia (2) - totalling 35 study rows, matching Fig3's flat list. Note the header is printed verbatim as 'South_Sudan' with an underscore, a Stata variable-name artefact, and is transcribed as printed. ANOMALY 1: South_Sudan and Sudan each contain exactly one study and NO Subtotal diamond is printed for either - the single study row stands alone. Their absent subtotals are therefore genuinely not printed (no row emitted), not missed. ANOMALY 2: the Zambia subtotal label prints Stata MISSING-VALUE dots verbatim - 'Subtotal  (I^2 = .%, p = .)' - i.e. the heterogeneity statistics are printed as missing rather than as numbers. Its diamond is also drawn much smaller/narrower than the other subtotal diamonds, and its CI (0.52, 0.57) is narrower than either contributing study's CI (0.49 [0.46,0.52] and 0.68 [0.63,0.72]) and its point estimate 0.55 lies between them - a pooled CI narrower than every input CI with missing I2 is statistically anomalous for a 2-study random-effects fit and is flagged here for review; the values are recorded exactly as printed and were NOT corrected. ANOMALY 3: the Kenya subtotal (0.64 [0.19, 1.09]) and the Rwanda subtotal (0.55 [0.16, 0.95]) have upper/lower bounds outside the admissible [0,1] range for a proportion - Kenya's upper bound 1.09 exceeds 1. Panels distinguished via the `subgroup` field; they are four SEPARATE meta-analyses, not subgroups of one pooled analysis. The top-level `heterogeneity` block carries PANEL A ONLY (I2=99.1%, tau2=1.2674, p=0); B (I2=98.4%, tau2=1.1590, p<0.0001), C (I2=99.3%, tau2=5.3040, p<0.0001) and D (I2=7.7%, tau2=1.7882, p=0.3682) are recorded verbatim as `heterogeneity` rows under their own subgroup — the schema has one top-level slot and the four panels must not be merged. No weight column is printed anywhere (square size only), so weight_pct is null throughout.\n\nROW_TYPE — THE CRITICAL CALL: each row is a STATE, not a study. The columns are 'State | No. of studies | n | N', and 'No. of studies' is >1 for most rows (e.g. Odisha in panel A aggregates 103 studies, Madhya Pradesh 56, Jharkhand 48).
